2027-05-09.title: Seventh Sunday of Resurrection (the Sunday after the Ascension)
2027-05-09.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Matthias is added to the eleven apostles
Every tongue shall confess that Jesus Christ is Lord
Go into all the world and proclaim the good news
2027-05-09.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta), in the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost. The Sunday after the Ascension (Thursday 6 May), and the third day of the novena to the Holy Spirit. Longer forms in the calendar: Philippians 1:27–2:11 and Mark 16:9–20. In the Latin Church in India the Ascension of the Lord is celebrated today, in place of the Seventh Sunday of Easter. Many dioceses also keep the World Day of Social Communications on this Sunday before Pentecost (verify locally).
2027-05-09.verse: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
theo: This is the Sunday after the Ascension. Three days ago we watched the Lord taken up; next Sunday we will celebrate the coming of the Spirit. Today the Church stands in between, and the four readings tell one story: the Lord who reigns in glory sends people out. The Gospel of Mark ends with that double movement. The Risen Lord appears to the eleven “as they were sitting at the table”; he reproaches them for their unbelief, and then, astonishingly, he entrusts the whole world to these same slow-hearted men: “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.” Then “the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.” And the last verse of the Gospel says: “they went out and proclaimed the good news everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the message by the signs that accompanied it.” The Lord is seated in heaven and working on earth at the same time. That is the meaning of the Ascension for the Church: he has not gone away from his work; he does it now through us. One of those eleven was Thomas, and the good news he carried reached our shores. Every Syro-Malabar Christian who hears this Gospel is the fruit of that sending.

The first reading shows us the throne from which the sending comes. “In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lofty; and the hem of his robe filled the temple.” The seraphs cry to one another: “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.” We sing that hymn in every Holy Qurbana, joining the angels before the throne of the One who has ascended. Isaiah's first response is fear: “Woe is me! I am lost, for I am a man of unclean lips.” Then a seraph touches his lips with a live coal from the altar, and says, “your guilt has departed and your sin is blotted out.” Syriac Fathers such as St Ephrem saw in that coal, taken from the altar with tongs and placed on the lips, a figure of the Holy Qurbana, the fire of the Lord's Body given to us. Only after he is purified does Isaiah hear the question: “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And he answers, “Here am I; send me!” The mission that follows is hard: the people will not listen, the land will be laid waste. Yet the chapter ends with hope: “The holy seed is its stump.” God never abandons his people; from the stump of Jesse the Messiah will come.

The Acts of the Apostles shows the Church obeying that sending in the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. Just before today's reading we hear that the apostles “were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus” (Acts 1:14). Then Peter stands up among about a hundred and twenty believers. The circle of the Twelve has been broken by the betrayal of Judas, and it must be restored before the Spirit comes. The one chosen must be a witness: “one of the men who have accompanied us during all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us, beginning from the baptism of John until the day when he was taken up from us, one of these must become a witness with us to his resurrection.” They propose two, Joseph called Barsabbas and Matthias. They do not campaign; they pray: “Lord, you know everyone's heart. Show us which one of these two you have chosen.” The lot falls on Matthias, “and he was added to the eleven apostles.” Here, in the presence of Mary, we see the apostolic Church taking care for its own continuity: the ministry of the apostles is handed on. Our bishops stand in that same line of witnesses, and the Synod of our Church still begins its elections with prayer to the Lord who knows every heart.

Paul's letter to the Philippians sings the whole mystery we are celebrating. “Let the same mind be in you that was in Christ Jesus, who, though he was in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to be exploited, but emptied himself, taking the form of a slave, being born in human likeness.” He went down, all the way to the Cross. “Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend, in heaven and on earth and under the earth, and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.” The Ascension is that exaltation made visible: the One who emptied himself now sits at the right hand of God. But Paul did not write this hymn only to tell us about Christ; he wrote it to change the way the Philippians lived together. “Do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility regard others as better than yourselves.” The way up for the Church is the way Christ went: the way down, in humility and service. A parish quarrelling about positions, a family where everyone wants the first place, will not proclaim the Gospel well. A community that has the mind of Christ will be sent, like Isaiah and like the eleven, and the Lord will work with it.
conn: Before the throne the living creatures sing without ceasing, “Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty, who was and is and is to come” (Revelation 4:8).
John says of Isaiah's vision: “Isaiah said this because he saw his glory and spoke about him” (John 12:41).
“A shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots” (Isaiah 11:1).
“All these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus, as well as his brothers” (Acts 1:14).
Jesus promised the Twelve that they would sit “on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel” (Matthew 19:28): the number of the apostles is restored before Pentecost.
God swears in Isaiah: “To me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear” (Isaiah 45:23); Paul applies it to Jesus.
“The LORD says to my lord, ‘Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool’” (Psalm 110:1).
Thomas, among the eleven who heard “Go into all the world”, is honoured by our Church as the apostle who brought the Gospel to India.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana we sing with the seraphs, “Holy, holy, holy”, before the throne of the Lord who has ascended. And like Isaiah we receive on our lips the live coal from the altar: the Body and Blood of Christ, which take away our guilt and make us ready to be sent.
At the end of the Qurbana we are sent out, as the eleven were sent. The Lord who is seated at the right hand of God goes with us and works with us through the week.
outline: Between the Ascension and Pentecost: the Lord in glory sends people out.
Isaiah's vision, the live coal, and “Here am I; send me!”
Point 2 · One must become a witness
Matthias, the hundred and twenty, and Mary in the upper room.
Point 3 · He emptied himself, therefore God exalted him
The hymn of Philippians and the humility of the Church.

The commissioning, the Ascension, and the Lord who works with us.
A small fishing boat at Kodungallur, where tradition says Thomas landed, and a Gospel that crossed the sea.
live: Sing the Holy, holy, holy with attention (Isaiah 6:3)
At the Qurbana today, sing the angels' hymn slowly, knowing you stand before the throne of the Ascended Lord.
Offer the Lord one concrete service in your parish or neighbourhood this week, and tell your priest or a parish leader.
Pray daily this week for the bishops of the Syro-Malabar Synod, successors of the apostles, that the Lord who knows every heart may guide them.
In one quarrel or competition at home or at work, choose to give the first place to the other.
Send a word of faith, a Gospel verse or an invitation to the Qurbana to one person who has drifted away; use the media well on this Sunday of social communications.
fathers: The seraph did not touch the coal with his fingers but took it with tongs; yet to us the Lord gives the fire into our own hands and onto our lips. The coal that touched Isaiah's lips forgave his sins; the Bread that is placed in our mouths, filled with fire and Spirit, makes us holy.

What was visible in our Redeemer has passed over into the sacraments. After the Ascension our faith grows stronger, because it no longer depends on sight: we believe in the One whom we do not see, seated at the right hand of the Father, and we meet him in the mysteries of the Church.
magis: Before the glory of the thrice-holy God, Isaiah cries out, “Woe is me! I am lost.” Before the holy God man discovers his own insignificance; yet God who is holy can forgive and purify.

The Lord's Body is taken up into heaven and he sits at the right hand of God: the inauguration of the Messiah's kingdom. Being seated at the Father's right hand signifies that he shares the glory and honour of the divinity.

The apostles took care to appoint successors, so that the mission entrusted to them might continue after their death; the bishops have by divine institution taken the place of the apostles as pastors of the Church.

The Word became flesh, emptying himself and taking the form of a servant; the hymn of Philippians 2 confesses that God has given him the name above every name, and that every tongue shall confess Jesus Christ as Lord.
The Church, sent by God to the nations, strives to preach the Gospel to all, obeying the missionary mandate of her founder.
saints: Seventh Sunday of Resurrection, the Sunday after the Ascension. In the Latin Church in India, the Ascension of the Lord. Third day of the novena to the Holy Spirit.

7–13 May: the days after the Ascension of our Lord (Thursday 6 May), when the apostles waited in prayer for the Holy Spirit “together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus” (Acts 1:14). Many families and parishes pray a novena to the Holy Spirit from Friday 7 to Saturday 15 May, the eve of Pentecost. Fri 7: First Friday. Sun 9: Seventh Sunday of Resurrection, the Sunday after the Ascension; the Latin Church in India celebrates the Ascension on this Sunday. Mon 10: in the Latin calendar, St John of Avila. Wed 12: in the Latin calendar, Sts Nereus and Achilleus and St Pancras. Thu 13: in the Latin calendar, Our Lady of Fatima. The Marian month of May continues (verify locally).
16 May: Pentecost, First Sunday of the Apostles; the Season of the Apostles begins.
2027-05-09.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you emptied yourself and became obedient unto death, and the Father has exalted you and seated you at his right hand. With the seraphs we cry, Holy, holy, holy. Touch our lips with the live coal of your altar, take away our guilt, and make us answer, Here am I; send me. Guide the successors of your apostles as you guided the choice of Matthias. Give us your mind, humble and loving, so that our communities may proclaim you. Work with us, Lord, wherever you send us, until every tongue confesses that you are Lord, to the glory of the Father. With Mary your Mother we pray: send us your Holy Spirit. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Isaiah sees the Lord on his throne, is purified by a live coal, and says, “Here am I; send me!”
Acts: in the presence of Mary and the apostles, Matthias is chosen as a witness to the Resurrection.

2027-05-09.action: Offer the Lord one concrete service in your parish this week, and say to him: Here am I; send me.
2027-05-09.question: If the Lord asked me today, “Whom shall I send?”, what would I answer?
catechism: The Ascension and the right hand of the Father.
kidsaint: Isaiah lived in Jerusalem about seven hundred years before Jesus. One day in the Temple he saw God on a great throne, with angels singing, “Holy, holy, holy!” Isaiah felt small and sinful, but an angel touched his lips with a burning coal and made him clean. Then God asked, “Whom shall I send?” and Isaiah said, “Here am I; send me!” Isaiah wrote many beautiful promises about Jesus, the Saviour who would come. Lesson: when God asks for a helper, you can say, ‘Here I am!’
2027-05-09.special: Seventh Sunday of Resurrection, the Sunday after the Ascension. In the Latin Church in India, the Ascension of the Lord. Third day of the novena to the Holy Spirit.
term: The hymn of the seraphs in Isaiah 6:3, sung in the Eucharistic prayer of every ancient rite. In the Syro-Malabar Qurbana it is sung in the anaphora after the priest recalls the angels who praise God; the people join the heavenly worship, and the hymn continues with “Hosanna in the highest” and “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord”. It reminds us that the Qurbana is offered before the throne of the Lord who has ascended.

family.explain: Isaiah saw God in the Temple, and he felt that he was not good enough. An angel took a burning coal from the altar and touched his lips, and Isaiah was made clean. Then God asked, “Whom shall I send?” and Isaiah said, “Here am I; send me!” Jesus too sent his friends before he went up to heaven: Go into all the world! Today Jesus asks each of us to be his helper.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries, and for all who tell others about Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Where can each of us say ‘Here I am, send me’ this week: at home, at school, at work?”

illus: At Kodungallur, where an old tradition says the apostle Thomas landed in AD 52, a group of catechism children once asked their teacher how one man from Galilee could bring the faith so far. She took them to the shore and pointed at the small fishing boats going out. ‘He came on a ship like a trader,’ she said, ‘but he carried something no trader carried. He had heard the Lord say, Go into all the world, and he believed it.’ One boy asked, ‘Who will go now?’ The teacher smiled. ‘The Lord is still asking the same question he asked Isaiah: Whom shall I send? Some of you will go across the sea. Most of you will go across the road to a neighbour. Both are the same mission.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, seated at the right hand of the Father, you send your disciples into all the world. As we gather with Mary in prayer, touch our lips and our hearts, and make us ready to be sent. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts (Isaiah 6:3). When have I felt the holiness of God, in the Qurbana or in prayer?
Woe is me! I am lost, for I am a man of unclean lips (Isaiah 6:5). What do I need the Lord to purify before I can serve him?
Lord, you know everyone's heart (Acts 1:24). How do we make important decisions as a family or a group: with prayer, or without?
Let the same mind be in you that was in Christ Jesus (Philippians 2:5). Where do I seek the first place for myself?
Go into all the world and proclaim the good news (Mark 16:15). Who is the Lord sending me to this week?
pm.resp: Here am I, Lord; send me.
interc: For the Church, that in these days before Pentecost she may be renewed in her mission to all the world.
For Pope Leo and our bishops, successors of the apostles, that the Lord who knows every heart may guide them.
For missionaries from Kerala serving in India and in every continent, that the Lord may work with them and confirm their words.
For those who work in the media and social communications, that they may serve the truth and the dignity of every person.
For those who feel unworthy to serve, that the Lord may purify them and send them.
For our parish, that we may have the mind of Christ and serve one another in humility.
pm.close: Father, you exalted your Son, who emptied himself for us, and seated him at your right hand. Make us witnesses to his Resurrection, humble in our life together and generous in our mission, and send us the Holy Spirit he promised, through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, on Thursday we celebrated the Ascension, and next Sunday we will celebrate Pentecost. Today we stand in between, and the readings tell us one thing: the Lord who reigns in glory sends his people out.

Isaiah sees the Lord on a high throne, and the angels singing, “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts.” We sing that same hymn at every Holy Qurbana. Isaiah is afraid: “Woe is me! I am lost, for I am a man of unclean lips.” An angel touches his lips with a burning coal from the altar, and his sin is taken away. Our Syriac Fathers saw in that coal a picture of the Holy Qurbana, placed on our lips. Then God asks, “Whom shall I send?” And Isaiah answers, “Here am I; send me!”

In Acts, the apostles are praying with Mary, the mother of Jesus. Judas is gone, and the circle of the Twelve must be complete before the Spirit comes. They choose a witness to the Resurrection. They do not make speeches; they pray: “Lord, you know everyone's heart.” Matthias is chosen. The work of the apostles is handed on. Our bishops stand in that line today. Let us pray for them.

Paul sings of Jesus, who “emptied himself, taking the form of a slave”, and went down to the Cross. “Therefore God also highly exalted him.” The Ascension is that exaltation. But Paul says: let the same mind be in you. Do nothing from selfish ambition. Regard others as better than yourselves. The Church goes up the way Christ went: by going down in humility and service.

In the Gospel the Risen Lord scolds his disciples for their unbelief, and then he sends these same weak men: “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.” He is taken up into heaven, and “they went out and proclaimed the good news everywhere, while the Lord worked with them.” He is in heaven and at work on earth at the same time.

Thomas was one of those eleven. Because he went, we are here. Now the Lord asks each of us: Whom shall I send? Maybe across the sea, maybe across the road to a neighbour. Let us answer with Isaiah: Here am I; send me. And let us pray with Mary this week for the Holy Spirit, who will give us the strength to go. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Isaiah heard God ask, “Whom shall I send?” and he said, “Here am I; send me!”

Before Jesus went up to heaven, he sent his friends to tell everyone about him. Jesus wants you to be his helper too. This week, can you tell one friend something good about Jesus? Say to him: ‘Here I am, Jesus!’

intro: Theme: “Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, ‘Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?’ And I said, ‘Here am I; send me!’”
On the Sunday after the Ascension: the thrice-holy God who purifies and sends, the witness chosen in prayer with Mary, the self-emptying and exaltation of Christ, and the mission to all the world.

Purified at the altar and praying with Mary, let us answer: Here am I; send me.
